title: MetaV: A Meta-Verifier Approach to Task-Agnostic Model Fingerprinting

problem.claim: Model piracy forensics needs methods for determining whether a suspect deep neural network was stolen from an original model.

gap.claim: Existing model fingerprinting schemes rely heavily on classification-task characteristics, limiting application to more general scenarios.

contributions.claim: MetaV is a task-agnostic model fingerprinting framework designed to fingerprint a wider range of deep neural networks independently of the downstream learning task.
MetaV combines an adaptively learned fingerprint with a meta-verifier that jointly determine whether a suspect model is stolen from outputs on the adaptive fingerprint.
The fingerprinting process does not assume model internals, provided ensemble models have the same input and output dimensions.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across classification, regression, and generative modeling, the authors report that MetaV substantially improves performance over state-of-the-art fingerprinting schemes and has enhanced generality.
For ResNet-18 trained for skin cancer diagnosis, the authors report 100% true positives and 100% true negatives on a diverse test set of 70 suspect models.
In the reported skin-cancer-diagnosis example, MetaV achieves an approximately 220% relative improvement in ARUC over the optimal baseline.

narrative_sequence.summary: Deep neural network intellectual-property protection is an urgent concern for information-technology corporations.
Prior model fingerprinting methods use adversarial examples built for the owner's model and compare behavioral patterns between original and suspect models.
Those methods are constrained by their dependence on classification-task characteristics.
MetaV addresses the limitation through an adaptive fingerprint and jointly optimized meta-verifier, without requiring model-internal assumptions beyond matching input and output dimensions.

Experiments spanning classification, regression, and generative modeling report improved performance and generality, including perfect reported true-positive and true-negative rates in one 70-model example.

source_observation.claim: A fingerprinting system can be made task-agnostic by adapting the fingerprint and learning a verifier from suspect-model outputs.

interpretation.claim: Separating task-independent evidence collection from learned ownership verification may broaden applicability across model families and task types.

application.claim: For model-ownership audits, consider interfaces based on shared input and output dimensions rather than task-specific internals.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish effectiveness when models lack matching input and output dimensions or under conditions outside the reported experiments.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the adaptive fingerprint construction or meta-verifier architecture.
The abstract does not detail the ownership obfuscation techniques tested or their individual effects.
The abstract does not provide datasets, baseline configurations, statistical uncertainty, or independent verification procedures.
